svg.title: A real solution tower A = (Aj) evaluates these symbols in its real coordinates. Evaluation separates polynomials by the finite-variable argument of (PF1). The restriction map from radial labels substitutes the radial potential reconstructed from Aj into each original jet coordinate. Its kernel at horizon d is exactly the equation ideal: it consists of polynomials vanishing on every such solution tower. Its image Winv d is the invariant sector of weight at most d. To see surjectivity onto this sector, use the color-equivariant projection of radial curvature coefficients onto their Maxwell subspace and then radial reconstruction to lift every linear solution coordinate. Polynomial substitution preserves weight and equivariance; restriction of this lift is the identity. This is an algebraic operation on coefficients, not a claim about interacting equations.
